 Follow Netflix Launches The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez Trailer for 4-Part Podcast
 Anubhav Chaudhry Thu, November 12, 2026 at 6:52 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Photo Credit: @Netflix / YouTube Netflix dropped the first trailer for The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez , a four-part video podcast event hitting the platform later this month. The series features host Angie Martinez finally sharing a nearly 30-year-old interview with Tupac Shakur alongside notable guests from the hip-hop world.
 The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez trailer revealed
 Netflix has released the official trailer for The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez. The four-part video podcast event arrives on the streaming platform on November 27. Radio Hall of Famer Angie Martinez recorded an interview with Tupac Shakur in 1996, just months before his death.
 Martinez held onto unreleased portions of that conversation for nearly 30 years. She told Netflix's Tudum that the rapper "reached out about me appearing in his 'I Ain't Mad at Cha' video." Martinez declined but agreed to visit Los Angeles for an in-person interview at his home. She recalled that Tupac "had New York pizza waiting for me when I arrived because he wanted me to feel at home."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The host explained her long silence about the full recording in the Tudum interview. "There were things said in that conversation that could have hurt people, damaged relationships, and added fuel to an already dangerous situation," Martinez said. She aired only select portions at the time and kept the rest private.
 Martinez now believes the tapes deserve a wider audience. "I also realized these tapes were bigger than me," she told Tudum. "They're a piece of hip-hop history, and I don't think they should just sit in my possession forever." She added that the four-part format allows her to share them with proper context.
 The series features guests including Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden, Big Boy, Dream Hampton, RZA, and Wallo. Matt Barnes, Bootleg Kev, E.D.I. Mean, Lil' Cease, Monie Love, and Ed Lover also appear. Martinez, Brittany Ortiz, Barnes, Brian Dailey, Stephen Jackson, Jelani McCoy, and Christina Mizzi serve as executive producers. IRL Productions and All the Smoke Productions produce the project.
 The Tupac Tapes With Angie Martinez premieres November 27 on Netflix.
